newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says all its allies are pressured by China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says all its allies are pressured by China.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister, on the eve of a damage-control trip to estranged ally South Africa, said on Sunday Taipei must guard against rival Beijing's plot to lure away the island's few remaining allies.
Minister John Chang said China had not only been courting Taiwan's bigger partners such as Panama, it had also wooed minor states like Saint Christopher.
"There is not a single country that we have diplomatic ties with that mainland China is not trying to court," Chang said in an interview by the state-run Taiwan Television.

Taiwan is now recognised by only 29 countries -- mostly underdeveloped states in central America and Africa -- since Pretoria's announcement last week that it would switch recognition to mainland China.
"We have to be careful about all our allies, not only Panama but also small countries like Saint Christopher," Chang added.

Seeking to salvage highest possible unofficial links after the Pretoria fallout, Chang will leave for South Africa on Monday on a five-day trip that will include meetings with South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo.
It remains uncertain whether Chang will also hold talks with President Nelson Mandela, who announced Pretoria's diplomatic switch on November 27.
Taipei has blamed Mandela's decision on efforts by Beijing to turn Taiwan into an international pariah.
China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province unentitled to foreign recognition since the two split at the end of the civil war in 1949.

Beijing, which threatens to attack Taiwan if it tries to declare independence, intensified its containment policy after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui made a private but high-profile visit to the United States in 1995.

China mounted intimidating war games in waters near Taiwan in the months leading up to the island's March presidential election, which Lee won in a landslide, and stepped up pressure on South Africa and other diplomatic allies of Taiwan to switch ties to Beijing.
